title: Console core vitals: MVP slice + scope reduction plan for dashboards, tracing, and cost cards
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
This ticket captures a concrete scope reduction and acceptance criteria for the Console observability surface (dashboards, tracing entrypoints, and per-route cost breakdown). After stakeholder review and early engineering estimates, we need to deliver a smaller, production-safe MVP slice that de-risks rollout and preserves the most customer-facing value: fast diagnosis of latency and cost regressions for production routes.

Goals (MVP slice):
- Deliver a single ‘Core Vitals’ dashboard card set per route: throughput, p50/p95 latency, and error rate (30d, 7d, 1d rollups).
- Surface a lightweight cost breakdown card for routes showing token-cost estimate (normalized $/1k tokens) and 7d trend with simple attribution to model and route tags.
- Provide a tracing link: a one-click jump from a route row to sampled distributed traces in the tracing system (no full trace UI embedded).
- Keep retention and heavy analytics out of MVP: no long-term raw log retention, no per-token tokenization flamecharts, and no complex cohort filters.

Scope removals (explicit cuts):
- Remove: per-token cost drilldown and per-token latency waterfall (deferred to post-MVP).
- Remove: full embedded trace explorer. MVP will open traces in the existing tracing service at a pre-populated filter.
- Remove: advanced cohort analysis (tag combinators, funnel-style breakdowns).
- Reduce: rollup retention for dashboard aggregates to 30 days in UI (backend will keep 90d for future work but not surfaced).

Trade-offs and rationale:
- Time-to-value: Customers mainly need fast detection of cost and latency regressions and a link to investigate; deep exploratory tooling can be developed later.
- Engineering risk: Avoid integrating a new trace UI and long-term storage in this release to reduce infra and compliance scope.
- Observability economics: Limiting retention and sampling reduces platform cost and error blast radius for early adopters.

Engineering deliverables / responsibilities:
- ENG-20345 (Telemetry ingestion): provide 7d/30d/1d aggregates and route tagging stable API. (Owner: Priya Nair)
- ENG-20567 (Cost estimator): return normalized per-route cost estimate endpoint with 7d trend. (Owner: Marco Rivera)
- ENG-20812 (Tracing linker): surface route -> trace filter URL generator and ensure SSO passthrough. (Owner: Yasmin Okoye)
- Console UI: build Core Vitals cardset, route table affordances, and single-click trace link (Owner: Liam Chen)

Acceptance criteria (must be met to mark Done):
- Core Vitals card appears on route detail and routes list for customers in the beta cohort.
- P50 and P95 latency charts render with < 250ms UI latency for the default 7d window.
- Cost card shows a 7d trend and a normalized $/1k tokens number; values match Cost Estimator API within 5% on sampled routes.
- Trace link opens external tracing UI with route and time-range pre-populated and preserves SSO for enterprise customers.
- Feature flag gating: the surface must be behind a console_observability_mvp flag that can be toggled per-org.
- E2E tests: automated smoke tests that validate card render, cost API integration, and trace link generation exist in the console CI.
- Documentation: PRD link, screenshots, and Quick Start instructions exist in Confluence and are referenced in the release notes.

Acceptance metrics (post-launch):
- Adoption: 10% of active routes for beta orgs have Core Vitals accessed at least once in first 14 days.
- Regression detection time: median time-to-first-investigation (dashboard -> trace) < 10 minutes after anomaly alert (where anomaly is >30% p95 increase).

Rollout plan:
- Canary (week 1): enable for internal orgs + 2 pilot customers. Collect telemetry and heatmap of most-used cards.
- Beta (week 2–4): open to selected customers via support opt-in.
- GA gating: pass stability SLOs (95% card render success rate, no > 10% increase in console error budget) and security review for SSO flows.

Docs & links:
- PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/console/core-vitals-mvp
- Design mocks: https://drive.google.com/designs/console-core-vitals-2026
- Cost estimator RFC: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/128
- Related Linear tickets: ENG-20345, ENG-20567, ENG-20812
acceptance_criteria: Core Vitals card renders on route detail and routes list
Latency charts (p50/p95) load under 250ms for default 7d window
Cost card shows normalized $/1k tokens and 7d trend; delta vs Cost API < 5%
Trace link opens external tracing UI with time-range and route filter; SSO preserved
Feature is gated behind console_observability_mvp per-org flag
Automated E2E smoke tests for render, cost integration, and trace link exist
PRD, screenshots, and Quick Start docs published in Confluence
comments: 2026-03-10 Aisha Patel: Created initial slice after product review. Pinned ENG tickets and requested triage meeting.
2026-03-11 Liam Chen: Reviewed with Eng. Proposed to defer per-token waterfall and full trace explorer to Q2 to reduce infra work. Updated estimate to 5 pts.
2026-03-12 Priya Nair: Telemetry team can provide 7d/30d rollups; backend will keep 90d for later surfacing. Noted sampling constraints for p95 accuracy.
2026-03-12 Marco Rivera: Cost estimator will expose normalized metric; need to finalize currency normalization rules (link to RFC).
2026-03-13 Yasmin Okoye: Confirmed SSO passthrough approach for trace link; flagged an edge-case where orgs use separate trace tenants (follow-up ENG-21001).
2026-03-13 Product Review: Stakeholders approved scope cuts and the release gating criteria. Proceed to canary once ENG tickets start landing in CI.
